title: Why production incidents recur
brief: Post-incident reviews generate actions; few are completed and fewer are verified. Analyses the failure pattern, distinguishes mitigation from cause removal, and gives a closure standard for corrective actions.

title: Kubernetes support windows and the cost of deferred upgrades
brief: Upstream and managed-service support windows turn a deferred upgrade into a dated risk with a price. Covers current support policies from research, removed APIs, add-on compatibility, and an upgrade readiness evidence model.

title: Findings closed, exposure open: remediation versus verification
brief: The gap between a closed ticket and a closed exposure. Catalogues how fixes fail to hold (rebuild from old image, reverted configuration, partial rollout, exception never expired) and defines closure criteria based on re-test.

title: How identity controls drift
brief: Identity policy rarely fails by being removed; it fails by accumulating exceptions. Traces the common drift paths in enterprise tenants and defines effective-coverage measures that expose them.

title: Standing privilege and the evidence gap
brief: Access reviews certify that privilege exists, not that it is needed. Compares attestation evidence with usage evidence and sets out a privilege model based on eligibility, time-bound elevation and recorded justification.

title: Non-human identity exposure
brief: Service principals, keys, tokens and now agent identities have no joiner-mover-leaver process. Covers inventory, ownership, credential age, federation in place of secrets, and how AI agents enlarge the population.

title: Data freshness is an AI quality problem
brief: An AI system with a stale corpus answers confidently and wrongly. Traces lag from source to index, shows why pipeline success hides age, and sets out consumer-defined freshness thresholds and deletion propagation.

title: What change failure rate proves, and what it does not
brief: The metric is easy to flatter. Covers current definitions from research, what counts as a failed change, measurement traps, pairing with recovery time and rework, and using it as a threshold rather than a scorecard.

title: Cloud commitments and utilisation risk
brief: Commitment discounts convert variable cost into a fixed obligation that architecture change can strand. Covers coverage and utilisation as paired thresholds, expiry tracking, and commitment decisions ahead of migrations. Uses current instrument names from research.

title: Continuous assurance is not monitoring
brief: Monitoring reports what a system is doing; assurance states whether an agreed outcome is still proven and who acts when it is not. Compares monitoring, audit, managed service and assurance across evidence, threshold, ownership and closure.

title: Assurance is a state, not a report
brief: The founding argument of the category. Point-in-time attestation describes the past; the four-state model (assured, degrading, at risk, unassured) describes now. Explains evidence expiry and why 'unassured' is distinct from 'failing'.
